name: Overpass API (OpenStreetMap query)
summary: Read-only query language API to extract any OpenStreetMap features by tag, area or bounding box.
description: Run Overpass QL queries to fetch nodes, ways and relations with tags and geometry, for example all cafes in a bounding box, roads, boundaries or amenities. Output as JSON, XML or CSV; supports 'out geom' for full geometry and area filters.

auth.notes: No key. Send a descriptive User-Agent with a real contact: the server answers 406 to generic clients (curl, browsers' default strings) and to placeholder contacts such as example.com.

required_headers.name: User-Agent
required_headers.notes: Name your app and give a real URL or e-mail. Generic or placeholder values (curl/x.y, Mozilla/5.0, anything containing example.com) returned HTTP 406 on 2026-11-11.

rate_limit.summary: Fair use: about 10,000 queries/day and 1 GB/day per server suggested; slots limit concurrent queries (see /api/status).

endpoints.summary: Run an Overpass QL query (form-encoded data parameter)

agent_notes: Send the query as form field data=<Overpass QL>. Set [out:json] and [timeout:N], keep bounding boxes small (south,west,north,east order), and send a User-Agent that names your app and a real contact. Retry 502s with backoff.
caveats: Requests without a User-Agent, with a generic one, or with a placeholder contact (example.com) are rejected with HTTP 406 by the front-end nginx.

The public instance is often at capacity: on 2026-11-11 it alternated between HTTP 502 (Markdown body: all query workers busy, retry with exponential backoff) and connection timeouts with no response. Back off and retry; check /api/status before batch jobs; run your own instance for heavy use.
Overpass QL has a learning curve.

verification.notes: Exact POST example with this User-Agent returned 200 (JSON, CORS *) several times on 2026-11-11 via curl; later runs of bin/verify.php hit 502/timeouts while the server was at capacity.
